research:
I've finished the research. My summary below uses only information published on or before 2026-08-20.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the first published NSA value for the week ending 2026-09-05 in the DOL weekly claims report, which is FRED series ICNSA. That figure should come out in the DOL release of Thursday 2026-09-10.
- 2026-08-20: The latest DOL release covers the week ending Aug 15. Advance NSA claims were about **172,080**, down 17,123 (-9.1%) from 189,203 the week before. The prior week was revised up from the 186,909 in the code baseline. SA claims were 206,000, down 6,000. The prior week was revised to 212,000 from 209,000, and the 4-week SA average is 204,000. [DOL via govdelivery](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDOL/bulletins/425f7f5); [oui.doleta.gov](https://oui.doleta.gov/press/2026/081326.pdf)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The target week is three weeks after the latest data point.
- Calendar note: Labor Day 2026 is Monday Sept 7, so the week ending Sept 5 is the **week before Labor Day**. Claims in that week usually hold flat to slightly lower than late August. The big seasonal drop comes in Labor Day week itself.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-20: SA claims fell to 206k (week ending Aug 15), and NSA fell to about 172k. SA claims are still low by historical standards. [govdelivery](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDOL/bulletins/425f7f5)
- 2026-07 to 08: NSA claims went from a peak of 246,015 (week ending Jul 11, the auto-retooling and summer layoff season) to 193,403 (Jul 18), 176,535 (Jul 25), 172,472 (Aug 1), 189,203 (Aug 8) and about 172,080 (Aug 15, advance). [FRED ICNSA](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/ICNSA.txt)
- I found no news of special factors such as fraud spikes, strikes or storms affecting the target week.

## 4. Base rates
NSA claims (FRED ICNSA, revised values) from about mid-August to the week before Labor Day:

| Year | Mid-Aug week (3 wks prior) | Week before Labor Day | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025 | Aug 9: 199,390 | Aug 30: 196,712 | -1.3% |
| 2024 | Aug 10: 200,837 | Aug 31: 190,623 | -5.1% |
| 2023 | Aug 12: 213,803 | Sep 2: 191,353 | -10.5% |
| 2022 | Aug 13: 187,391 | Sep 3: 172,835 | -7.8% |
| 2021 | Aug 14: 309,229 | Sep 4: 285,683 | -7.6% |

- Matching by calendar date instead of the holiday, the Aug 16-20 week to the Sep 6-10 week, gives: 2025 194,217 to 204,862 (+5.5%, the week ending Sep 6, 2025 was Labor Day week and had a Texas fraud spike), 2024 192,455 to 178,682 (-7.2%), 2023 199,517 to 175,594 (-12.0%), 2022 179,211 to 152,144 (-15.1%). These target weeks were Labor Day weeks, and Labor Day weeks run lower. That makes them a weaker analog for 2026.
- This year is running **below** recent years. Mid-August 2026 NSA (about 172k) is roughly 11% below 2025 (194k), about 10% below 2024 and close to 2022 (179k for the week ending Aug 20).
- Applying the -1% to -10.5% before-Labor-Day changes to 172,080 gives about 154k to 170k. Scaling 2025's week before Labor Day (196,712) by the year-on-year ratio (about 0.89) gives about 175k. The recent 2026 August weeks moved between 172k and 189k.
- The code baseline (median 184.8k, p10 147k, p90 229k) is built from the Aug 8 value of 186,909, which has since been revised up to 189,203, and the next print was lower. The baseline also does not account for the week falling just before the holiday.
- Advance NSA figures usually get revised by a few hundred to about 2,500 claims. Only the first print counts here.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on NSA claims for this week. Kalshi's weekly jobless claims markets are on the SA headline figure.
- Economists' consensus forecasts are on SA claims and were around 205-215k for recent weeks. I found no consensus for the target week yet.
- The DOL seasonal factors for the week ending Sep 5, 2026 are published ahead of time on the DOL claims page. I could not pull the exact factor, but it is normally around 0.85 to 0.90 for the week before Labor Day. With that factor, SA claims of about 205k would imply NSA of roughly 175-185k. This is my rough approximation, and the factor should be checked.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-27: DOL release for the week ending Aug 22.
- 2026-09-03 (Thursday): DOL release for the week ending Aug 29.
- 2026-09-04: August employment report from BLS.
- 2026-09-10: DOL release with the advance figure for the week ending Sep 5, which resolves the question. The Labor Day holiday on Sep 7 could shift the release timing or state reporting, but releases usually stay on Thursday.
- Risks: Atlantic hurricane season is near its peak, and Gulf or Southeast landfalls have pushed state claims up before (for example Florida, Louisiana, North Carolina). I did not get the latest NOAA outlook. Other risks are state-level fraud spikes, as in Texas in September 2025, and back-to-school layoffs of education support staff in some states.
